finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: the `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands with the server's privileges.

trace.note: Route GET /ping; req.query.host is attacker-controlled, no auth middleware on the app
Value concatenated into shell string and run via exec (/bin/sh -c)
Only err is checked; output is returned via res.send(out)
app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds to all interfaces

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, regex, quoting/escaping, or argv-form execFile on the path. The err check on line 8 only handles failures and does not restrict input. No auth middleware is applied to the route. Query values may be arrays, which concatenate to comma-joined strings and do not block injection. Sibling routes /version and /uptime use constant commands, so they are not affected.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6-7 takes req.query.host and concatenates it straight into the exec() shell string with no validation, escaping, or execFile argv form. The only check, tools.js:8, only handles errors and does not restrict input. No auth middleware is registered anywhere: tools.js is the only file in the directory and the route is declared directly on app at tools.js:6. Sibling routes at tools.js:15-26 use constant commands and are not affected.
verdict.reason: The GET /ping route at tools.js:6-7 passes attacker-controlled req.query.host into exec() (which runs via /bin/sh -c) with no guard, and app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 exposes it without authentication, so an anonymous attacker can inject shell metacharacters such as `;` or `$(...)` to run arbitrary commands.
